chapter: Third reel: musicians and George Girard
title: Musicians he is proud to have worked with
summary: He lists Monk Hable, Harry Shields, Sharkey, Al Hirt, Pete Fountain, Tony Mitchell and praises Jim LaRocca and Connie Jones.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You know Dick, I really feel very good of having had the opportunity of working with fellas like the late Monk Hable, the late Larry Shields, and Jeff Riddick, and the late Almond Hug. Which Shields? Larry Shields. Harry Shields.

Harry, yeah. Larry is his brother who passed away many years ago. Now Larry, the one that was in California, he wrote clarinet, marmalade, plus many other tunes. Oh. No, I'm talking about having had the pleasure of working with the late Monk Hazel, the late Harry Shields, and the late Almond Hug, and of course the late Sharky's. I feel really honored having had the opportunity of working with guys like that. And of course I really enjoyed working with Al Hurd and Pete Fountain, and of course Bob Havens and all those jazz greats. And of course Raymond Boyk, who I have a lot of respect for. And Tony Mitchell, I can't leave Tony out. Tony's a marvelous musician, marvelous clarinet player. And you know who I think is a very fine trumpet man? It's Jim LaRocka. I love Jim LaRocka's playing. He's a powerhouse like Al Hurd.
I haven't heard him in years.

Jim is, and I understand he's coming back in the famous store. He's gonna take over the group that's on a night shift, which was formerly Tommy Yedda's group. You know, Tommy Yedda left about a month ago. And I'm glad to see Jim LaRocka come back. He plays a lot of trumpet. To me, he's one of the finest young trumpet men around. He's a powerhouse, I tell you.
There's so many that I like, and so many that it seems to me never really gone places. For example, I enjoy Connie Jones' playing.
And he knows tunes like, I'll Be a Friend with Pleasure. One day I just wanted to bug him and I asked him for that. He knew it.
